title: Predictable Dedicated: Q2 Plan for Autoscaling Policies, Burst Pricing, and Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Quarter plan to deliver predictable autoscaling for Dedicated pools. Goal: provide deterministic throughput and transparent cost behavior when customers use autoscale/burst, with rollout controls and observability baked into Console and API. This ticket captures product scope, acceptance criteria, milestones, dependencies, and stakeholder alignment for the quarter.
progress_updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff workshop with Eng (Serving, Orchestration), Console PM, Design. Collected top customer asks: predictable tail latency, explicit burst caps, and immediate billing visibility for bursts.
2026-03-04: Drafted initial product requirements and shared canonical Confluence doc (link below). Asked Eng to validate feasibility of per-pool burst tokens vs dynamic GPU autoscaling.

2026-03-09: Architecture review with runtime leads. Agreed to two-phase approach: Phase A = soft autoscale policies (burst pools + throttles) + Console controls; Phase B = runtime-integrated fast-scaling (hot-add instances) pending kernel scheduling improvements.
2026-03-12: Design handed over mid-fidelity mocks for Console UX: per-pool autoscale slider, burst budget forecast, and post-burst invoice preview. Requested design review cycle this week.
decisions: Adopt two-phase delivery: (A) Policy & UX first to give customers control and visibility; (B) Runtime fast-scaling as a follow-up depending on infra work and SLOs.
Burst capacity will be represented as 'burst tokens' scoped to a pool and time window rather than unlimited spontaneous GPU additions to avoid immediate capacity chase and billing surprises.
Billing model for burst will be hybrid: customers pay for reserved units as before; bursts consume burst tokens and are charged at a defined premium rate visible in Console before enabling.
Canary rollout strategy: enable autoscale toggles for 5 pilot customers using a feature-flagged policy and dedicated monitoring dashboards before general availability.
review_feedback: Design (Maya Lopez): Requested clearer error states in Console when burst tokens exhausted and CTA to request more capacity/support.
Eng (Runtime lead, Diego Ramos): Recommended API schema extension to include 'capacity_hint' and 'billing_hint' fields to ease routing and cost estimation.
Security (Priya Singh): Requested threat modelling for inter-pool routing and confirmation that KMS-managed keys are not exposed by new autoscale telemetry exports.
milestones: M1 2026-03-21: Product spec finalized + design mocks approved
M2 2026-04-15: API schema PR and Console prototypes merged to staging
M3 2026-05-20: Pilot rollout to 5 customers + monitoring dashboards active
M4 2026-06-30: GA release with billing visibility and docs
acceptance_criteria: Customers can configure per-pool autoscale policy and burst budget in Console and via API
Burst consumption is visible in near real-time in Console with projected cost estimates
Pilot customers report <=5% increased tail latency during bursts and no silent overloads
Billing records expose burst usage line-items and invoice preview matches pilot telemetry
Feature gated behind release flag; rollback path documented
stakeholders: Engineering: Samir Chen (Lead PM Eng liaison), Diego Ramos (Runtime), Lin Zhao (Orchestration)
risks: Runtime can’t reliably hot-add capacity in Phase A — mitigated by token-based burst model
Billing reconciliation complexity if telemetry lags — mitigated by invoice preview and chargeback testing
Customer confusion around pricing — mitigated with in-Console previews and in-product tooltips
Potential security audit for telemetry exports — schedule security review early
notes: Follow-up meeting 2026-03-16 to prioritize API fields and finalize migration plan for existing Dedicated customers.
Coordinate with Pricing for correct SKU mapping; finance to provide acceptance test cases for invoice previews.
Document fallback behaviors when burst tokens exhausted (queueing, throttling, graceful degradation) in runbook.
